topic_tag: a harbor painting in a provincial museum
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.

worlds.passage: A small canvas of a harbor at dawn, painted in 1874, hangs in a provincial museum among the painter's other early work. That spring a critic wrote that the young painter would never equal the old Dutch masters, whom the critic revered and the painter found dull. He answered by painting the harbor in the exact manner of one of them, darkening the varnish with smoke and letting a dealer sell it as a lost original; once the critic had praised it in print, the painter produced his sketches, then went back to painting as before. Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.
worlds.explanation: Passing the canvas off as a lost Dutch original to trap a critic made it his "hoax." "Homage" fails because he found those masters dull and was answering the critic, not honoring them; "hybrid" fails because it copies one master's exact manner; "landmark" fails because he went back to painting as before.

homage.why: he did not mean to honor masters he found dull

hybrid.quote: in the exact manner of one
hybrid.why: a single style imitated exactly is not a blend

landmark.quote: went back to painting as before
landmark.why: it marked no turn in his career

worlds.passage: A small canvas of a harbor at dawn, painted in 1874, hangs in a provincial museum among the painter's other early work. His teacher, who died that spring, had been known above all for one harbor at dawn. The painter set up his easel on the same quay, followed that composition stroke by stroke in the teacher's manner, signed it with both their names, and hung it in his studio, where it stayed unsold while he went back to painting as before. Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.
worlds.explanation: Recreating his late teacher's most famous scene and signing both names is a tribute, so the canvas was his "homage." "Hoax" fails because the double signature deceived no one; "hybrid" fails because it follows the teacher's manner alone; "landmark" fails because he went back to painting as before.

hoax.quote: signed it with both their names
hoax.why: an openly credited recreation deceives no one

hybrid.quote: stroke by stroke in the teacher's manner
hybrid.why: one borrowed manner, not a mixture

landmark.quote: went back to painting as before
landmark.why: it changed nothing in his career

worlds.passage: A small canvas of a harbor at dawn, painted in 1874, hangs in a provincial museum among the painter's other early work. He collected the cheap Japanese woodblock prints then arriving at the port by the crate, and in this one canvas their flat colors and black outlines sit inside the deep, measured perspective he had been drilled in at the academy. He signed it openly, sold it to a neighbor, and went back to painting as before; no other picture of his tries the mixture again. Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.
worlds.explanation: Print-style color and outline set inside academic perspective make the canvas his "hybrid." "Hoax" fails because he signed it openly; "homage" fails because its sources were anonymous prints bought by the crate and his own schooling, not a figure he honored; "landmark" fails because no other picture of his tries the mixture again.

hoax.why: an openly signed work deceives no one

homage.quote: arriving at the port by the crate
homage.why: cheap anonymous prints are a source of technique, not a person paid tribute

landmark.quote: no other picture of his tries
landmark.why: a one-off with no successors is not a turning point

worlds.passage: A small canvas of a harbor at dawn, painted in 1874, hangs in a provincial museum among the painter's other early work. Until that spring he had painted in the smooth, polished manner taught at the academy, and the harbor began that way too. Halfway through, he scraped the whole canvas down and repainted it in short, broken strokes of unmixed color, a method he had seen nowhere; he signed it openly, and nothing he painted in the forty years after returns to the polished manner. Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.
worlds.explanation: The canvas where he abandoned the academic manner, never to return to it, is his "landmark." "Hoax" fails because he signed it openly; "homage" fails because the method was one he had seen nowhere; "hybrid" fails because he scraped the whole canvas down, replacing the old manner rather than blending it.

homage.quote: a method he had seen nowhere
homage.why: it imitates and honors no one

hybrid.why: one style replaced another; they were not combined
